heme_involvement_pattern.primary_compartment: bone_marrow (clonal plasma cells producing amyloidogenic light chains)
characteristic_organ_involvement: heart (restrictive cardiomyopathy — common presenting feature; cardiac involvement in ~50-70% at diagnosis)
soft tissue (macroglossia — highly suggestive/pathognomonic when present)

biomarkers.name: Tissue biopsy with Congo red staining + green birefringence
biomarkers.clinical_use: Confirms amyloid deposition. Fat pad, rectum, kidney, or affected organ biopsy

biomarkers.name: Amyloid typing (mass spectrometry preferred; IHC alternative)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Distinguishes AL (light chain) from ATTR (transthyretin), AA (serum amyloid A), and rarer forms — critical because treatment differs

biomarkers.name: Serum FLC + FLC ratio
biomarkers.prevalence: Usually abnormal; monoclonal light chain production is required for AL
biomarkers.clinical_use: Difference between involved and uninvolved FLC (dFLC) is a Mayo staging component in revised systems and is used for haematologic response monitoring

biomarkers.name: NT-proBNP + Troponin T (or hs-TnT)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Cardiac staging is biomarker-based. In Mayo 2004, thresholds include NT-proBNP >332 pg/mL and cTnT >0.035 μg/L. In the European/Mayo 2012 modification, stage III is split using NT-proBNP >8500 pg/mL; in the revised Mayo 2012 system, dFLC ≥180 mg/L is added to troponin and NT-proBNP to create stages I-IV

biomarkers.name: CD38, t(11;14)
biomarkers.prevalence: CD38 commonly expressed on clonal plasma cells; t(11;14) ~40-60%
biomarkers.clinical_use: Daratumumab (dara-CyBorD — ANDROMEDA) is a first-line standard. t(11;14) is enriched in AL and is associated with sensitivity to BCL2 inhibition; venetoclax is promising but not an established regulatory-standard therapy specifically for AL

biomarkers.name: Cardiac MRI with LGE (late gadolinium enhancement)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Diffuse subendocardial or transmural LGE is characteristic of cardiac amyloidosis

biomarkers.name: Bone scintigraphy (99mTc-DPD/PYP/HMDP)
biomarkers.prevalence: Usually strongly positive in ATTR; can be negative or occasionally positive in AL
biomarkers.clinical_use: Grade 2-3 uptake with negative monoclonal workup strongly supports ATTR (often no biopsy needed). Helps distinguish ATTR from AL, but positive uptake does not by itself exclude AL when a monoclonal gammopathy is present

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Tissue deposition of amorphous eosinophilic material (light chain-derived amyloid) with characteristic apple-green birefringence under polarised light after Congo red staining
variants: by involved organ: cardiac AL, renal AL, hepatic AL, GI AL, autonomic AL, systemic multiorgan AL
histomorphological_subtype.grading: Mayo cardiac staging (stage I-IV in revised systems) drives prognosis

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Underlying clonal plasma cell disorder produces amyloidogenic light chains — treatment targets the plasma cell clone (dara-CyBorD — ANDROMEDA); t(11;14) is enriched in AL and may predict venetoclax sensitivity
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Perivascular and diffuse amyloid deposition in affected organs; cardiac AL shows diffuse subendocardial or transmural LGE pattern on MRI

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Plasma cells producing amyloidogenic light chains — often small underlying clone (may be MGUS-level plasma cell burden)
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Terminal plasma cell differentiation similar to MGUS/SMM (often low plasma cell burden); distinctive feature is production of amyloidogenic light chains (particularly lambda) that misfold and deposit as amyloid fibrils in tissues
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Amyloidogenic light chain production is defining biology — biased immunoglobulin light chain variable gene usage has been associated with organ tropism, including cardiac involvement; t(11;14) is enriched in AL (~40-60%) compared with MM and may contribute to venetoclax sensitivity
